**Visible content.** A single spheroid rendered as a dense cluster of pale "pearl" spheres, ringed by ~40 orange ellipsoids (CAFs) scattered around the exterior. Counter reads "356 living tumor cells · whole volume"; header labels the condition "01 / CAF secretion · uptake intact". Scale bar "50 µm, focal plane" top-right; timestamp "0 min" bottom-right; footnote "Exterior · CAF shape is illustrative".

**Field and legend.** The legend lists Living tumor · pearl, CAF, Dead tumor · violet, and an Alanine ramp with ticks 0 · 0.51 · 1.01 mM, marked "fixed shared range". No alanine colour is actually painted in the viewport — Field opacity is at 0%, so the nutrient field is invisible; only the legend swatch shows the ramp. No violet cells are visible, so the dead category appears empty at this frame.

**Concrete defects.** (1) Field opacity 0% makes the alanine legend non-actionable. (2) Only the exterior shell is visible; interior cells are fully occluded by the outer sphere layer, so the 356 "whole volume" count cannot be verified from pixels. (3) CAF glyph shape is declared illustrative, not measured. (4) Time is 0 min — a single frame. (5) "Paired comparison" is unchecked, so no contrast field is shown.

**Spatial effect.** Only one: CAFs sit outside the tumour mass, none embedded within it. No radial gradient, core hypoxia, or uptake asymmetry is visible.

**Not inferable.** Alanine exchange or uptake between CAF and tumour, death rates, growth over time, condition-versus-control differences, and any core state. The scales cannot exaggerate differences here because no differences are rendered.

observation.observation:
**Visible tissue.** A single spheroid, cutaway at z ≤ 0 µm, viewed in "Core" mode at frame 1440 min. Two cell states are legible against the legend: violet "dead tumor" spheres dominate the mass (roughly the entire right/central bulk), while pearl "living tumor" spheres form a small crescent confined to the upper-left rim — consistent with the header count "57 living tumor cells · whole volume." Orange spindle CAFs sit outside the ball as a sparse ring, none embedded within it.

**Nutrient field.** The alanine field is essentially invisible in the main viewport at 30% field opacity; only the inset "exact voxel slice" carries signal, a flat teal square with mild edge banding. Its readout states 0.0100–0.0320 mM against a fixed shared 0–0.1 mM bar, 0 saturated voxels — so the rendered colour occupies only the bottom third of the ramp and does not exaggerate contrast; if anything it compresses it.

**Defects.** Field opacity too low to read spatially in 3D; the inset is heavily pixelated with no numeric ticks on the colour bar; near-side violet spheres occlude the pearl crescent's depth extent and hide the core interior; CAF spindles clip the spheroid silhouette; nearest voxel centre is z 10.0 µm, not the requested z 0 µm, so the inset slice is offset from the cutaway plane.

**Spatial effect.** Only one: living cells are peripheral and asymmetric (one flank), dead cells central — a viability gradient. The inset field is too flat and too coarse to show any matching gradient.

**Not inferrable.** Whether CAF secretion causes the surviving crescent, whether uptake is genuinely "intact," any dose–response, and any difference versus the unrendered paired condition — the comparison checkbox is unticked and only one condition is displayed.

observation.observation:
**Visible tissue.** Two paired panels, same time stamp (1,440 min), cutaway z ≤ 0 µm, "Core" view. Both show a spheroid of densely packed violet spheres (legend: dead tumor · violet) ringed by orange elongated CAF bodies. Panel 01 ("CAF secretion · uptake intact", 57 living tumor cells) shows a small cluster of pale pearl spheres only on the left/upper-left rim — a dozen or so, all peripheral. Panel 02 ("Tumor uptake suppressed", 0 living) has no pearl cells at all; the two masses otherwise look nearly identical in size and packing.

**Nutrient field.** The alanine voxel-slice insets are almost uniformly flat teal in both panels, brighter in the interior square, with no visible gradient toward CAFs. Legend states a fixed shared range 0 · 0.05 · 0.1 mM; panel readouts give 0.0100–0.0320 mM and 0.0100–0.0321 mM, 0 saturated voxels. So the two conditions differ by ~0.0001 mM — the shared color scale does *not* exaggerate; it renders them indistinguishable, and the on-screen count difference (57 vs 0) is not mirrored by any visible field difference.

**Occlusion.** Severe: the inset panel covers the lower-right quadrant of each spheroid; the outer violet shell hides the entire core, so interior cell states are unobservable at this cutaway. Field opacity 30% further washes the overlay.

**Concrete defects.** (1) Insets occlude tissue and cannot be moved. (2) Field range spans only ~1/3 of the legend's 0–0.1 mM ticks, wasting the ramp. (3) No per-panel colorbar with actual min/max; numbers sit in small text. (4) Living-cell count is whole-volume while the render is a z ≤ 0 cutaway — count and picture are not the same sample. (5) No dead-cell count for comparison. (6) Pearl cells are one-sided, suggesting a seeding or boundary asymmetry that is unlabeled.

**Spatial effect.** Only one: surviving pearl cells are exclusively rim-adjacent on one flank in panel 01, adjacent to the CAF ring. That is a visible spatial association, not a demonstrated cause — the field slice shows no matching local enrichment, and the asymmetry could equally be an initialization artifact.

**Cannot be inferred from these pixels.**

- That CAF-secreted alanine rescues tumor cells. The ~0.0001 mM difference between panels is below any visible contrast; no gradient links CAFs to survivors.
- That uptake suppression *caused* the 57 → 0 drop. Both conditions are labeled, but the mechanism is off-screen; only the outcome counts differ.
- Anything about the spheroid interior. The intact violet shell and the inset occlusion hide every core cell, so claims about hypoxic centers, necrotic cores, or radial death gradients are unsupported.
- Timing or kinetics. A single frame at 1,440 min shows no trajectory; whether death was gradual or immediate is unknowable.
- Whether violet cells died or were seeded dead. No initial-condition frame is shown.
- Absolute concentrations as biology. Values are simulation output at one voxel slice, z-center 10.0 µm versus requested 0 µm — an admitted 10 µm mismatch between the field sampled and the tissue plane rendered.

**Smallest fixes, in order.** Move insets outside the render; print per-panel min/max on the colorbar; label counts as whole-volume versus slice; add the z-mismatch as a visible warning rather than fine print.
